name: Iktómi

domain_history.domain: spider-trickster/culture-hero figure, sometimes anthropomorphic, sometimes arachnid, shape-shifting; functions as a teaching/moral-instruction figure via trickster narratives

notes: Per James R. Walker's Pine Ridge material (Lakota Belief and Ritual, ed. DeMallie and Jahner, 1980/1991): one origin account describes Iktómi as a "fallen"/demoted figure — originally Kṡa, "god of wisdom," condemned by Škáŋ (god of motion) to a marginal, mischief-making existence after misusing his wisdom to shame others. This specific origin story is Walker's particular informant-derived version, not necessarily a pan-Lakota consensus account, and is sourced accordingly (MODERATE confidence on this specific episode; HIGH on the general trickster-figure documentation).
